items.title: Python range(): Represent Numerical Ranges
items.description: Master the Python range() function, see how it works under the hood, and learn when enumerate() or zip() beat ranges in your loops.
items.summary: In Python, the range() function generates a sequence of numbers, often used in loops for iteration . By default, it creates numbers starting from 0 up to but not including a specified stop value.

items.title: Python's Requests Library (Guide)
items.description: The Requests library is the go-to tool for making HTTP requests in Python. Learn how to use its intuitive API to send requests and interact with the web.
items.summary: The Requests library is the go-to package for making HTTP requests in Python. It abstracts the complexities of making requests behind an intuitive API .

items.title: How to Write Beautiful Python Code With PEP 8
items.description: Learn how to write readable, high-quality Python code by following the PEP 8 style guide and using linters and autoformatters to enforce it.
items.summary: PEP 8, sometimes spelled PEP8 or PEP-8, is the official style guide for Python code. PEP 8 gives guidelines on naming conventions, code layout, and other best practices.

items.title: Getters and Setters: Manage Attributes in Python
items.description: Learn what Python getter and setter methods are, why properties are usually the better choice, and when getters and setters still make sense.
items.summary: Getter and setter methods allow you to access and mutate non-public attributes while maintaining encapsulation . In Python, you’ll typically expose attributes as part of your public API and use properties when you need attributes with functional behavior.

items.title: Pyrefly: A Fast Static Type Checker for Python Projects
items.description: Learn how to use Pyrefly, a fast static type checker for Python, to catch type errors, generate type annotations, and measure type coverage.
items.summary: Pyrefly is a fast static type checker for Python that helps you catch type-related issues before running your code. It also includes features for generating type hints and measuring type coverage across a codebase.

items.title: Python Circular Imports: Why They Happen and How to Fix Them
items.description: Confused by Python circular imports? Learn why they happen, how Python's import system works, and how to fix import errors using practical examples.
items.summary: A Python circular import happens when two modules import each other and one of them isn’t finished loading yet. Python reports it as an ImportError or an AttributeError , usually with a message about a partially initialized module.

items.title: MCP vs API Calls: Which Should You Use for Python LLM Apps?
items.description: MCP vs API calls: build one Python tool, integrate it both ways, and compare. Learn what each approach costs and when an MCP server pays for itself.
items.summary: Anthropic open-sourced the Model Context Protocol (MCP) in November 2024 to fix a scaling problem: every new tool a model reached for needed its own integration, built on direct API calls. Building that integration today involves a decision usually framed as MCP vs API calls.

items.title: How to Get Out of Tutorial Hell
items.description: Stuck in tutorial hell? Learn how to get out by turning Python tutorials into practical projects that build real skills and lasting confidence.
items.summary: Tutorial hell is an unfortunate reality for many newcomers to Python, and learning how to get out of it starts with understanding why it’s so easy to fall into. When you’re a beginner, finishing tutorials is addictive!

items.title: Exploring AI Coding Agent Workflows
items.description: AI coding agents come in four types: IDE, terminal, PR, and cloud. Learn how each workflow fits into modern Python development.
items.summary: AI coding agents can read your code, reason about changes, and act on your behalf. To choose the right one, it helps to understand the four common workflow types: integrated development environment (IDE), terminal, pull request (PR), and cloud.

items.title: Learn With Mentor AI: A Guided Journey Through Async Python
items.description: Experience a new way of learning on Real Python by working through async Python in conversation with Mentor AI, one well-placed question at a time.
items.summary: I’d been writing Python for a couple of years before async programming made sense to me. I understood the general idea, but the syntax just never felt like Python.

items.title: Build a Python MCP Client to Test Servers From Your Terminal
items.description: Follow this Python project to build an MCP client that discovers MCP server capabilities and feeds an AI-powered chat with tool calls.
items.summary: Building an MCP client in Python can be a good option when you’re coding MCP servers and want a quick way to test them. In this step-by-step project, you’ll build a minimal MCP client for the command line.

items.title: Python's F-String for String Interpolation and Formatting
items.description: Python f-strings give you a readable, concise way to interpolate and format strings, and they beat .format() and the % operator on speed.
items.summary: Python f-strings offer a concise and efficient way to interpolate variables, objects , and expressions directly into strings. By prefixing a string with f or F , you can embed expressions within curly braces ( {} ), which are evaluated at runtime .

items.title: Get Started With Django: Build a Portfolio App
items.description: Build a Django example project step by step. You'll create a portfolio app and learn about models, views, templates, and the admin.
items.summary: Django is a powerful Python web framework for creating complex applications. It follows the Model-View-Template (MVT) architecture and includes built-in features like authentication, an admin interface, and database management.

items.title: Python's property(): Add Managed Attributes to Your Classes
items.description: Use Python's property() to add managed attributes to your classes, with validation, computed values, and caching, without breaking your API.
items.summary: The @property decorator simplifies the management of attributes in your Python classes . It allows you to control attribute access, enabling features such as data validation, lazy evaluation , and the creation of backward-compatible APIs without modifying the class’s public interface.

items.title: NumPy Tutorial: Your First Steps Into Data Science in Python
items.description: Follow this NumPy tutorial to learn how to create and manipulate arrays in Python and take your first steps into data science.
items.summary: NumPy is a Python library that provides a simple yet powerful data structure : the n-dimensional array . This is the foundation on which almost all the power of Python’s data science toolkit is built, and learning NumPy is the first step on any Python data scientist’s journey.

items.title: Python Metaclasses
items.description: How Python's metaclasses work as an OOP concept, what they are good for—and why you might want to avoid them in your own programs.
items.summary: The term metaprogramming refers to the potential for a program to have knowledge of or manipulate itself. Python supports a form of metaprogramming for classes called metaclasses .

items.title: What Is the Python Global Interpreter Lock (GIL)?
items.description: The Python GIL is a mutex that lets only one thread control the interpreter at a time. Learn how it shapes your program's performance.
items.summary: The Python Global Interpreter Lock or GIL , in simple words, is a mutex (or a lock) that allows only one thread to hold the control of the Python interpreter. This means that only one thread can be in a state of execution at any point in time.

items.title: A Python AI Tool Was Just Booby-Trapped With Key-Stealing Malware
items.description: Real Python's weekly AI news for October 17–23, 2026, explained in plain language: a booby-trapped Python AI tool, a PHP security fix, and PyTorch on TPUs.
items.summary: Real Python AI News · Weekly edition · The week of October 17–23, 2026 Stop Falling Behind on AI. New models, new prices, new agent tools, all the time.

items.title: Building Serverless Python Apps Using AWS Chalice
items.description: Build and deploy a serverless Python app with AWS Chalice, a microframework that ships your code to AWS Lambda and scales it for you.
items.summary: Shipping a web application usually involves having your code up and running on single or multiple servers. In this model, you end up setting up processes for monitoring, provisioning, and scaling your servers up or down.

items.title: Sets in Python
items.description: Learn to work effectively with Python sets: define set objects, explore the supported operations, and know when sets fit your code.
items.summary: Python provides a built-in set data type. It differs from other built-in data types in that it’s an unordered collection of unique elements.

items.title: Sending Emails With Python
items.description: Learn how to send emails with Python using SMTP, attach files, format HTML messages, and personalize bulk emails for your contact list.
items.summary: You probably found this tutorial because you want to send emails with Python to automate confirmation messages, password resets, or scheduled notifications. Python’s standard library covers the whole pipeline, from making a server connection to building the message and sending it to one or many recipients.

items.title: An Intro to Threading in Python
items.description: Learn how to use Python threading to run tasks concurrently, synchronize threads with locks and queues, and avoid race conditions and deadlocks.
items.summary: Python threading allows you to have different parts of your program run concurrently and can simplify your design. If you’ve got some experience in Python and want to speed up your program using threads, then this tutorial is for you!

items.title: Three Ways of Storing and Accessing Lots of Images in Python
items.description: Compare three ways of storing images in Python, as PNG files on disk, in LMDB, and in HDF5, with timings for reading and writing lots of images.
items.summary: Why would you want to know more about different ways of storing and accessing images in Python? If you’re segmenting a handful of images by color or detecting faces one by one using OpenCV, then you don’t need to worry about it.

items.title: Dictionaries in Python
items.description: Learn how dictionaries in Python work: create and modify key-value pairs using dict literals, the dict() constructor, built-in methods, and operators.
items.summary: Python dictionaries are a powerful built-in data type that allows you to store key-value pairs for efficient data retrieval and manipulation. Learning about them is essential for developers who want to process data efficiently.

items.title: Python String Formatting: Available Tools and Their Features
items.description: Learn how Python string formatting works with f-strings, the .format() method, and the modulo operator, plus the strengths of each tool.
items.summary: String formatting is essential in Python for creating dynamic and well-structured text by inserting values into strings. This tutorial covers various methods, including f-strings, the .format() method, and the modulo operator ( % ).

items.title: A Guide to Modern Python String Formatting Tools
items.description: Explore Python's modern string formatting tools, and learn to harness f-strings and the .format() method for interpolation and formatting.
items.summary: In modern Python, you have f-strings and the .format() method to approach the tasks of interpolating and formatting strings. These tools help you embed variables and expressions directly into strings, control text alignment, and use custom format specifiers to modify how values appear.

items.title: Alexa Python Development: Build and Deploy an Alexa Skill
items.description: Become an Alexa Python developer by building and deploying your own Alexa skill, a joke bot that responds to voice commands on Amazon Alexa devices.
items.summary: Smart home speakers were a novel idea just a couple of years ago. Today, they’ve become a central part of many people’s homes and offices and their adoption is only expected to grow.

items.title: Logging in Python
items.description: Go beyond print() with Python logging. Create your first logs, set levels and formats, and add handlers that grow with your projects.
items.summary: lets you record important information about your program’s execution. You use the built-in logging module to capture logs, which provide insights into application flow, errors, and usage patterns.

items.title: Python Modules and Packages – An Introduction
items.description: Explore Python modules and packages, the two mechanisms that make modular programming possible, and learn how imports find your code.
items.summary: This article explores Python modules and Python packages , two mechanisms that facilitate modular programming . Modular programming refers to the process of breaking a large, unwieldy programming task into separate, smaller, more manageable subtasks or modules .

items.title: Python REST APIs With Flask, Connexion, and SQLAlchemy – Part 3
items.description: Extend your Flask REST API with a SQLAlchemy one-to-many relationship that adds notes to people, and serve them through new API endpoints.
items.summary: Most modern web applications are powered by a REST API under the hood. That way, developers can separate the front-end code from the back-end logic, and users can interact with the interface dynamically.

items.title: Python's with Statement: Manage External Resources Safely
items.description: Understand Python's with statement and context managers to streamline the setup and teardown phases in resource management. Start writing safer code today!
items.summary: Python’s with statement allows you to manage external resources safely by using objects that support the context manager protocol. These objects automatically handle the setup and cleanup phases of common operations.

items.title: Python Code Quality: Best Practices and Tools
items.description: Python best practices for code quality: what makes code good, and the tools and strategies that keep it that way as a project grows.
items.summary: Producing high-quality Python code involves using appropriate tools and consistently applying best practices . High-quality code is functional, readable, maintainable, efficient, and secure.

items.title: Python REST APIs With Flask, Connexion, and SQLAlchemy – Part 2
items.description: Build a Flask REST API backed by a SQLite database. In part two of this series, you'll use SQLAlchemy and Marshmallow to persist and serialize data.
items.summary: Most modern web applications are powered by a REST API under the hood. That way, developers can separate the front-end code from the back-end logic, and users can interact with the interface dynamically.

items.title: Python's asyncio: A Hands-On Walkthrough
items.description: Explore how Python asyncio works and when to use it. Follow hands-on examples to build efficient programs with coroutines and awaitable tasks.
items.summary: Python’s asyncio library enables you to write concurrent code using the async and await keywords. The core building blocks of async I/O in Python are awaitable objects—most often coroutines—that an event loop schedules and executes asynchronously.

items.title: Single and Double Underscores in Python Names
items.description: Learn Python naming conventions with single and double underscores to design APIs, create safe classes, and prevent name clashes.
items.summary: Python has a few naming conventions that are based on using either a single or double underscore character ( _ ). These conventions allow you to differentiate between public and non-public names in APIs, write subclasses safely, prevent name collisions, and more.

items.title: Python Protocols: Leveraging Structural Subtyping
items.description: Learn how Python protocols bring static duck typing to your code and help you get the most out of type hints and static type checkers.
items.summary: In Python, a protocol specifies the methods and attributes that a class must implement to be considered of a given type. Protocols are important in Python’s type hint system , which allows for static type checking through external tools, such as mypy , Pyright , and Pyre .

items.title: Build Command-Line Interfaces With Python's argparse
items.description: Use Python's argparse module to build command-line interfaces for your scripts, with arguments, options, subcommands, and automatic help messages.
items.summary: When building Python command-line interfaces (CLI), Python’s argparse module offers a comprehensive solution. You can use argparse to create user-friendly command-line interfaces that parse arguments and options directly from the command line.

items.title: How to Use Generators and yield in Python
items.description: Build generator functions and generator expressions with the Python yield statement, and learn when lazy evaluation pays off.
items.summary: Have you ever had to work with a dataset so large that it overwhelmed your machine’s memory? Or maybe you have a complex function that needs to maintain an internal state every time it’s called, but the function is too small to justify creating its own class .

items.title: Create a Flask Application With Google Login
items.description: Build a Python Flask app with Google login so users can sign in with their Google account, and learn OAuth 2, OpenID Connect, and Flask-Login.
items.summary: You’ve probably seen the option for Google Login on various websites. Some sites also have more options like Facebook Login or GitHub Login .

items.title: 13 Project Ideas for Intermediate Python Developers
items.description: Try 13 Python project ideas for intermediate developers. Build web, GUI, and command-line apps that challenge you and make you a better Pythonista.
items.summary: Learning the basics of Python is a wonderful experience. But the euphoria of just learning can be replaced by the hunger for hands-on projects.

items.title: ChromaDB: Embeddings and Vector Databases in Python
items.description: Learn what embeddings and vector databases are, then store, query, and filter text with ChromaDB in Python and use it to give an LLM context.
items.summary: ChromaDB is an open-source vector database built for applications that use large language models (LLMs). LLMs like the ones behind OpenAI’s ChatGPT can reason about natural language processing (NLP) problems remarkably well, but on their own, they only know what appeared in their training data.

items.title: Managing Python Projects With uv: An All-in-One Solution
items.description: Learn how to create and manage your Python projects using uv, an extremely fast Python package and project manager written in Rust.
items.summary: The uv tool is a high-speed package and project manager for Python. It’s written in Rust and designed to streamline your workflow.

items.title: A Practical Introduction to Web Scraping in Python
items.description: Get started with Python web scraping: parse data from websites and interact with HTML forms using Beautiful Soup and MechanicalSoup.
items.summary: Python web scraping allows you to collect and parse data from websites programmatically. With powerful libraries like urllib , Beautiful Soup, and MechanicalSoup, you can fetch and manipulate HTML content effortlessly.

items.title: Quiz: Working With APIs in Python: Reading Public Data
items.description: Test your understanding of consuming REST APIs with Requests, from status codes and JSON to query parameters, authentication, and rate limits.
items.summary: In this quiz, you’ll test your understanding of Working With APIs in Python: Reading Public Data . By working through this quiz, you’ll revisit how requests and responses work, what common status codes mean, how to read JSON data, how to filter results with query parameters, and how to authenticate with an API key.

items.description: Build a Flask REST API with Connexion and Swagger UI in this three-part series. Part one lays the foundation of your application.

He also explains how Reddit’s teams have built about 700 prototypes, reached 100% adoption across UX and product, and developed a Figma-to-PRD workflow that makes engineering handoffs far more precise.

items.title: How to Automate Your Workflow With Claude Code Hooks
items.description: Learn how to use Claude Code hooks that auto-format your Python code after every edit, enforce your chosen tools, and ping you when a task finishes.
items.summary: When you pair with Claude Code, some steps shouldn’t be left to chance, and Claude Code hooks are how you lock them in. You want a heads-up when it finishes a long task, a guarantee that it sticks to your project’s approved tools, and a promise that every edit is formatted to your code standards, without repeating yourself each time.

items.title: How to Round Numbers in Python
items.description: Learn how Python's round() works, why it rounds 2.5 to 2, and how you can manage rounding errors with decimal, NumPy, and pandas.
items.summary: Rounding numbers in Python is an essential task, especially when dealing with data precision. Python’s built-in round() function uses the rounding half to even strategy, which rounds numbers like 2.5 to 2 and 3.5 to 4 .

items.title: Asynchronous Tasks With Django and Celery
items.description: Integrate Django and Celery with Redis as a message broker, and move slow work like sending email out of the request cycle.
items.summary: Celery is a distributed task queue that processes tasks asynchronously, so slow work doesn’t hold up your web app’s response. When you integrate Celery with your Django application, you can offload time-consuming tasks and keep your users from waiting.

items.title: Digging Deeper Into Django Migrations
items.description: Go beyond the basics of Django migrations: how they work under the hood, what the Django migrations table tracks, and what's inside migration files.
items.summary: You already understand the purpose of Django migrations and you’re familiar with fundamental usage patterns like creating and applying migrations. In this tutorial, you’ll dig deeper into the migration system and take a peek at some of its underlying mechanics, from the Django migrations table to the migration files themselves.
